fields.name: EEAR[11:8]
fields.text: EEPROM address, high bits: with EEARL, picks the byte in the 4 Kbyte EEPROM, addressed linearly from 0 to 4096. Undefined at reset; write a valid address before any EEPROM access.

fields.name: EEAR
fields.text: EEPROM address, low byte: with EEARH, picks the byte in the 4 Kbyte EEPROM, addressed linearly from 0 to 4096. Undefined at reset; write a valid address before any EEPROM access.

fields.name: EEDR
fields.text: EEPROM data: holds the byte to write to the EEPROM at the EEAR address, and after a read holds the byte read from that address.

fields.name: EEPM
fields.text: EEPROM programming mode: picks what a write of EEPE does, an atomic erase-and-write or an erase or a write alone. Writes to EEPM are ignored while EEPE is set; reset clears EEPM to 0b00 unless the EEPROM is busy programming.

rows: Erase and write in one atomic operation.

fields.name: EERIE
fields.text: EEPROM Ready interrupt enable: with the SREG I bit set, 1 enables the interrupt and 0 disables it; the interrupt requests continuously while EEPE is clear.

fields.name: EEMPE
fields.text: EEPROM master programming enable: with it at 1, an EEPE write of 1 inside the next four clock cycles programs the selected EEPROM address; with EEMPE at 0, setting EEPE does nothing. Hardware clears EEMPE four clock cycles after software sets it.

fields.name: EEPE
fields.text: EEPROM programming enable, the write strobe: with address and data set up, write EEPE to 1 within four clock cycles after setting EEMPE (written with EEPE at 0) to start the write. Before starting, wait for EEPE and SPMCSR.SPMEN to read 0; EEAR and EEDR may be written in either order. No EEPROM write can run while the CPU is writing Flash. An interrupt between setting EEMPE and setting EEPE makes the write fail, and an interrupt routine that touches EEAR or EEDR during another EEPROM access makes that access fail. Hardware clears EEPE when the write is done; setting EEPE halts the CPU for two cycles.

fields.name: EERE
fields.text: EEPROM read enable, the read strobe: with the address in EEAR, write 1 to read; the data is ready at once and the CPU halts for four cycles. While a write is in progress the EEPROM cannot be read and EEAR cannot be changed.

fields.name: SRE
fields.text: External memory interface enable: 1 turns on the interface and gives AD7:0, A15:8, ALE, WR and RD to it, overriding the DDR settings of those pins; 0 turns it off and returns the pins to normal port use.

fields.name: SRL
fields.text: Wait-state sector limit: splits the external memory space into a lower and an upper sector, each with its own wait-state bits. At the reset value of 0 the whole space is one sector, timed by SRW11 and SRW10.

values.text: One sector, 0x2200-0xFFFF, timed as the upper sector.

fields.name: SRW1
fields.text: Wait states for the upper sector of external memory (SRW11, SRW10).

values.text: One wait cycle in the read/write strobe.
Two wait cycles in the read/write strobe.
Two wait cycles in the read/write strobe, and one more before the next address is driven.

fields.name: SRW0
fields.text: Wait states for the lower sector of external memory (SRW01, SRW00).

values.text: One wait cycle in the read/write strobe.
Two wait cycles in the read/write strobe.
Two wait cycles in the read/write strobe, and one more before the next address is driven.

fields.name: XMBK
fields.text: External memory bus keeper enable: 1 makes AD7:0 hold the last driven value while the interface has them tri-stated; 0 turns the keeper off. It works whether or not SRE is set.

fields.name: XMM
fields.text: External memory high mask: with external memory enabled, Port C carries the high address byte; these bits release some or all Port C pins to normal port use when fewer address bits are needed. They also allow all 64 Kbytes of external memory to be reached.

registers.name: OSCCAL
registers.title: Oscillator Calibration Register
notes: Initial value of bits 7:0 printed as Device Specific Calibration Value.

fields.name: CAL
fields.text: Oscillator calibration for the calibrated internal RC oscillator: loaded with the factory value at reset and writable to change the frequency. CAL7 picks the low (0) or high (1) range, the two ranges overlapping so 0x7F runs faster than 0x80; CAL6:0 tune within the range, 0x00 slowest and 0x7F fastest. The oscillator times EEPROM and Flash writes, which may fail if it is calibrated above 8.8MHz while writing.

registers.name: CLKPR
registers.title: Clock Prescale Register
notes: Initial value of bits 3:0 printed as See Bit Description.

fields.name: CLKPCE
fields.text: Clock prescaler change enable: must be written to 1, with all other CLKPR bits written 0 at the same time, before CLKPS can be changed. Hardware clears it four cycles later or when CLKPS is written; writing it again within those four cycles neither extends the window nor clears the bit.

fields.name: CLKPS
fields.text: Clock prescaler select: the factor dividing the selected clock source down to the system clock, and so the clock of all synchronous peripherals; writable at run time. Reset loads 0000 with the CKDIV8 fuse unprogrammed and 0011 (divide by 8) with it programmed, as shipped; any value can be written whatever CKDIV8 is.

fields.name: SM
fields.text: Sleep mode select: which sleep mode the SLEEP instruction enters, with SE set. Standby modes are meant for use with an external crystal or resonator.

fields.name: SE
fields.text: Sleep enable: must be 1 for the SLEEP instruction to put the MCU to sleep.

fields.name: PRTWI
fields.text: Power reduction TWI: 1 stops the TWI clock and shuts the module down; the TWI must be initialised again after it is woken.

fields.name: PRTIM2
fields.text: Power reduction Timer/Counter2: 1 shuts down Timer/Counter2 in synchronous mode (AS2 = 0); when re-enabled it carries on as before.

fields.name: PRTIM0
fields.text: Power reduction Timer/Counter0: 1 shuts the module down; when re-enabled it carries on as before.

fields.name: PRTIM1

fields.name: PRSPI
fields.text: Power reduction SPI: 1 stops the SPI clock and shuts the module down; the SPI must be initialised again after it is woken.

fields.name: PRUSART0
fields.text: Power reduction USART0: 1 stops the USART0 clock and shuts it down; USART0 must be initialised again after it is woken.

fields.name: PRADC
fields.text: Power reduction ADC: 1 shuts the ADC down, which must be disabled first; with the ADC shut down the analog comparator cannot use the ADC input multiplexer.

fields.name: PRTIM5
fields.text: Power reduction Timer/Counter5: 1 shuts the module down; when re-enabled it carries on as before.

registers.title: MCU Status Register
notes: Initial value of bits 4:0 printed as See Bit Description.
The register summary gives its address as 0x54.

fields.name: JTRF
fields.text: JTAG reset flag: set when a reset comes from a 1 written to the JTAG Reset Register, which the AVR_RESET JTAG instruction selects. A power-on reset or a 0 written to it clears it.

fields.name: WDRF
fields.text: Watchdog reset flag: set by a watchdog reset. A power-on reset or a 0 written to it clears it.

fields.name: BORF
fields.text: Brown-out reset flag: set by a brown-out reset. A power-on reset or a 0 written to it clears it.

fields.name: EXTRF
fields.text: External reset flag: set by an external reset. A power-on reset or a 0 written to it clears it.

fields.name: PORF
fields.text: Power-on reset flag: set by a power-on reset and cleared only by writing 0. Reading and clearing MCUSR early in the program lets the flags tell which reset came next.

fields.name: WDIF
fields.text: Watchdog interrupt flag: set on a watchdog time-out when the watchdog is set up for interrupt. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. With SREG I and WDIE set, the time-out interrupt runs.

fields.name: WDIE
fields.text: Watchdog interrupt enable: with SREG I set, 1 enables the watchdog interrupt. With WDE clear the watchdog is in Interrupt Mode; with WDE set it is in Interrupt and System Reset Mode, where the first time-out sets WDIF, running the vector clears WDIE and WDIF and leaves System Reset Mode, and WDIE must be set again after each interrupt to stay. If the interrupt has not run by the next time-out, the system resets. WDTON = 0 means the fuse is programmed.

rows: Interrupt, then switch to System Reset Mode.

fields.name: WDP3
fields.text: Watchdog timer prescaler bit 3: with WDP2:0, sets the prescaling and so the time-out period while the watchdog runs.

fields.name: WDCE
fields.text: Watchdog change enable: must be set to clear WDE or change the prescaler bits, in a timed sequence; hardware clears it four clock cycles after it is written to 1.

fields.name: WDE
fields.text: Watchdog system reset enable: forced to 1 while MCUSR.WDRF is set, so WDRF must be cleared before WDE can be cleared.

fields.name: WDP2
fields.text: Watchdog timer prescaler bit 2: with the other WDP bits, sets the prescaling and so the time-out period while the watchdog runs.

fields.name: WDP1
fields.text: Watchdog timer prescaler bit 1: with the other WDP bits, sets the prescaling and so the time-out period while the watchdog runs.

fields.name: WDP0
fields.text: Watchdog timer prescaler bit 0: with the other WDP bits, sets the prescaling and so the time-out period while the watchdog runs.

fields.name: JTD
fields.text: JTAG interface disable: 0 leaves the JTAG interface enabled when the JTAGEN fuse is programmed, 1 disables it. To change it, write the new value twice within four cycles. It must not be changed while the on-chip debug system is in use.

fields.name: PUD
fields.text: Pull-up disable: 1 turns off all I/O port pull-ups, even on pins whose DDxn and PORTxn (0b01) would enable them.

fields.name: IVSEL
fields.text: Interrupt vector select: 0 puts the interrupt vectors at the start of Flash, 1 moves them to the start of the boot loader section, whose address the BOOTSZ fuses set. To change it, write IVCE to 1, then within four cycles write IVSEL while writing IVCE to 0. Interrupts are off from the cycle IVCE is set until after the instruction following the IVSEL write, or for four cycles if IVSEL is not written; SREG I is not touched. With vectors in the boot section and BLB02 programmed, interrupts are off while running from the application section; with vectors in the application section and BLB12 programmed, they are off while running from the boot section.

fields.name: IVCE
fields.text: Interrupt vector change enable: must be written to 1 before IVSEL can be changed; hardware clears it four cycles later or when IVSEL is written. Setting it disables interrupts.

fields.name: JTD
fields.text: JTAG interface disable: 0 leaves the JTAG interface enabled when the JTAGEN fuse is programmed, 1 disables it. To change it, write the new value twice within four cycles. It must not be changed while the on-chip debug system is in use.

fields.name: PUD
fields.text: Pull-up disable: 1 turns off all I/O port pull-ups, even on pins whose DDxn and PORTxn (0b01) would enable them.

fields.name: IVSEL
fields.text: Interrupt vector select: 0 puts the interrupt vectors at the start of Flash, 1 moves them to the start of the boot loader section, whose address the BOOTSZ fuses set. To change it, write IVCE to 1, then within four cycles write IVSEL while writing IVCE to 0. Interrupts are off from the cycle IVCE is set until after the instruction following the IVSEL write, or for four cycles if IVSEL is not written; SREG I is not touched. With vectors in the boot section and BLB02 programmed, interrupts are off while running from the application section; with vectors in the application section and BLB12 programmed, they are off while running from the boot section.

fields.name: IVCE
fields.text: Interrupt vector change enable: must be written to 1 before IVSEL can be changed; hardware clears it four cycles later or when IVSEL is written. Setting it disables interrupts.

fields.name: ISC3
fields.text: External interrupt 3 sense control: the level or edge on INT3 that requests the interrupt, when SREG I and the EIMSK bit are set. INT3:0 edges are registered asynchronously; pulses wider than the minimum pulse width interrupt, shorter ones may not. A low level must last until the current instruction ends, and keeps requesting while held. Changing the bits can raise an interrupt, so disable INTn in EIMSK first, then change, then clear INTFn by writing 1 before re-enabling.

fields.name: ICNC1

fields.name: WGM2
fields.text: Low two bits of the waveform generation mode. With TCCR2B.WGM22 they choose the counting sequence, where the TOP value comes from, and the waveform type: normal, CTC, or one of two PWM modes. MAX is 0xFF; BOTTOM is 0x00.

fields.name: FOC2A
fields.text: Writing 1 forces an immediate compare match on the waveform generator, and OC2A changes as COM2A1:0 directs. Acts only in non-PWM modes; write it 0 whenever TCCR2B is written in a PWM mode. It is a strobe: the COM2A1:0 value at that moment decides the effect. A forced compare raises no interrupt and does not clear the timer in CTC mode with OCR2A as TOP. Always reads 0.

fields.name: FOC2B
fields.text: Writing 1 forces an immediate compare match on the waveform generator, and OC2B changes as COM2B1:0 directs. Acts only in non-PWM modes; write it 0 whenever TCCR2B is written in a PWM mode. It is a strobe: the COM2B1:0 value at that moment decides the effect. A forced compare raises no interrupt and does not clear the timer in CTC mode with OCR2B as TOP. Always reads 0.

fields.name: WGM22
fields.text: Top bit of the waveform generation mode; works with TCCR2A.WGM21:0.

fields.name: CS2
fields.text: Chooses the clock that drives Timer/Counter2. Where an external pin mode is used, edges on the T0 pin clock the counter even if that pin is set as an output, which lets software drive the count.

values.text: No clock; the timer is stopped.

fields.name: TCNT2
fields.text: Timer/Counter2 count value.

fields.name: OCR2A
fields.text: Timer/Counter2 output compare value A.

fields.name: OCR2B
fields.text: Timer/Counter2 output compare value B.

fields.name: EXCLK
fields.text: With the asynchronous clock selected, writing 1 turns on the external clock input buffer so a clock can drive TOSC1 in place of a 32kHz crystal. Write EXCLK before choosing asynchronous operation. The crystal oscillator runs only while EXCLK is 0.

fields.name: AS2
fields.text: 0: Timer/Counter2 runs from the I/O clock, clkI/O. 1: it runs from a crystal oscillator on TOSC1. Changing AS2 may corrupt TCNT2, OCR2A, OCR2B, TCCR2A and TCCR2B.

fields.name: TCN2UB
fields.text: Goes to 1 when TCNT2 is written while Timer/Counter2 runs asynchronously; hardware clears it once TCNT2 has taken the value from its temporary register. 0 means TCNT2 can take a new value.

fields.name: OCR2AUB
fields.text: Goes to 1 when OCR2A is written while Timer/Counter2 runs asynchronously; hardware clears it once OCR2A has taken the value from its temporary register. 0 means OCR2A can take a new value.

fields.name: OCR2BUB
fields.text: Goes to 1 when OCR2B is written while Timer/Counter2 runs asynchronously; hardware clears it once OCR2B has taken the value from its temporary register. 0 means OCR2B can take a new value.

fields.name: TCR2AUB
fields.text: Goes to 1 when TCCR2A is written while Timer/Counter2 runs asynchronously; hardware clears it once TCCR2A has taken the value from its temporary register. 0 means TCCR2A can take a new value.

fields.name: TCR2BUB
fields.text: Goes to 1 when TCCR2B is written while Timer/Counter2 runs asynchronously; hardware clears it once TCCR2B has taken the value from its temporary register. 0 means TCCR2B can take a new value. Writing one of the five Timer/Counter2 registers during its busy flag may corrupt the value and cause an unintended interrupt. Reading TCNT2 gives the live count; reading OCR2A, OCR2B, TCCR2A or TCCR2B gives the temporary register's content.

fields.name: OCIE2B
fields.text: With this bit at 1 and SREG's I-bit set, Timer/Counter2's interrupt for compare match B is on; it runs when TIFR2.OCF2B is set.

fields.name: OCIE2A
fields.text: With this bit at 1 and SREG's I-bit set, Timer/Counter2's interrupt for compare match A is on; it runs when TIFR2.OCF2A is set.

fields.name: TOIE2
fields.text: With this bit at 1 and SREG's I-bit set, Timer/Counter2's overflow interrupt is on; it runs when TIFR2.TOV2 is set.

fields.name: OCF2B
fields.text: Set to 1 by a compare match between Timer/Counter2 and OCR2B. Hardware clears it when the interrupt vector runs; writing 1 to it also clears it. With SREG's I-bit, OCIE2B and OCF2B all 1, the compare match interrupt runs.

fields.name: OCF2A
fields.text: Set to 1 by a compare match between Timer/Counter2 and OCR2A. Hardware clears it when the interrupt vector runs; writing 1 to it also clears it. With SREG's I-bit, OCIE2A and OCF2A all 1, the compare match interrupt runs.

fields.name: TOV2
fields.text: Set to 1 when Timer/Counter2 overflows; in PWM mode it is set when the counter turns around at 0x00. Hardware clears it when the interrupt vector runs; writing 1 to it also clears it. With SREG's I-bit, TOIE2 and TOV2 all 1, the overflow interrupt runs.

fields.name: TSM
fields.text: Timer/Counter Synchronization Mode.

fields.name: PSRASY
fields.text: Writing 1 resets the Timer/Counter2 prescaler. Hardware normally clears the bit straight away; in asynchronous mode it stays 1 until the prescaler reset is done. Hardware does not clear it while TSM is 1.

fields.name: PSRSYNC
fields.text: Prescaler reset for the synchronous Timer/Counters.

fields.name: SPIE
fields.text: Makes the SPI interrupt run when SPSR.SPIF is set and SREG's global interrupt enable is set.

fields.name: SPE
fields.text: 1 turns the SPI on; no SPI operation happens without it.

fields.name: DORD
fields.text: 1: the data word goes out LSB first. 0: MSB first.

fields.name: MSTR
fields.text: 1 selects master mode, 0 slave mode. If SS is an input and is pulled low while MSTR is 1, MSTR clears and SPSR.SPIF sets; software must set MSTR again to return to master mode.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: 1: SCK idles high. 0: SCK idles low.

fields.name: CPHA
fields.text: Picks the SCK edge that samples data: the leading (first) or the trailing (last).

fields.name: SPR
fields.text: Sets the SCK rate, against the oscillator clock fosc, when the device is master; no effect in slave mode.

registers.name: SPSR
registers.title: SPI Status Register
notes: The settings of SPI2X are carried on SPCR.SPR, which holds the low bits.

fields.name: SPIF
fields.text: Set when a serial transfer completes, and also when SS is an input pulled low in master mode. Raises an interrupt when SPCR.SPIE and global interrupts are on. Hardware clears it when the interrupt vector runs; otherwise it clears on a read of SPSR with SPIF set followed by an access to SPDR.

fields.name: WCOL
fields.text: Set when SPDR is written during a transfer. Cleared, together with SPIF, by a read of SPSR with WCOL set followed by an access to SPDR.

fields.name: SPI2X
fields.text: 1 doubles the SCK frequency in master mode, so the shortest SCK period is two CPU clocks. As a slave, the SPI is guaranteed only up to fosc/4. The SPI port also carries serial download and upload of program memory and EEPROM.

fields.name: SPDR

fields.name: RXC0
fields.text: 1 while the receive buffer holds unread data, 0 once it is empty. Disabling the receiver flushes the buffer, which clears RXC0. It can raise the Receive Complete interrupt (RXCIE0).

fields.name: TXC0
fields.text: Set when the whole frame in the transmit shift register has gone out and UDR0 holds no new data. Cleared automatically when the Transmit Complete interrupt runs, or by writing 1 to it. It can raise the Transmit Complete interrupt (TXCIE0).

fields.name: UDRE0
fields.text: 1 when the transmit buffer UDR0 is empty and can take new data. Set after reset to show the transmitter is ready. It can raise the Data Register Empty interrupt (UDRIE0).

fields.name: FE0
fields.text: 1 when the next character in the receive buffer arrived with a frame error, meaning its first stop bit was 0; 0 when that stop bit was 1. Holds until UDR0 is read. Write 0 here on every write to UCSR0A.

fields.name: DOR0
fields.text: 1 when a data overrun is seen: the receive buffer is full with two characters, a further character sits in the receiver's shift register, and another start bit comes in. Holds until UDR0 is read. Write 0 here on every write to UCSR0A.

fields.name: UPE0
fields.text: 1 when the next character in the receive buffer arrived with a parity error while parity checking was on (UPM01 = 1). Holds until UDR0 is read. Write 0 here on every write to UCSR0A.

fields.name: U2X0
fields.text: Acts in asynchronous mode only; write 0 in synchronous mode. 1 cuts the baud rate divisor from 16 to 8, doubling the asynchronous transfer rate.

fields.name: MPCM0
fields.text: 1 turns on multi-processor communication mode: the receiver drops every incoming frame that carries no address information. The transmitter is not affected.

fields.name: TWBR
fields.text: Division factor of the bit rate generator, the frequency divider that makes the SCL clock in the master modes.

fields.name: TWINT
fields.text: Set by hardware when the TWI finishes its current job and waits for software. With SREG's I-bit and TWIE set, the MCU jumps to the TWI interrupt vector. The SCL low period is stretched while TWINT is 1. Software clears it by writing 1; running the interrupt routine does not clear it. Clearing it starts the TWI, so all TWAR, TWSR and TWDR accesses must be done first.

fields.name: TWEA
fields.text: Controls the acknowledge pulse. With TWEA at 1, ACK is driven on the bus when the device's own slave address arrives, when a general call arrives with TWAR.TWGCE set, or when a data byte arrives in Master Receiver or Slave Receiver mode. Writing 0 temporarily cuts the device off the bus; writing 1 again resumes address recognition.

fields.name: TWSTA
fields.text: Written to 1 to become bus master: the TWI sends a START if the bus is free, or else waits for a STOP and then sends a new START. Software must clear TWSTA once the START has gone out.

fields.name: TWSTO
fields.text: In master mode, writing 1 puts a STOP on the bus, and the bit clears itself once the STOP is done. In slave mode, writing 1 recovers from an error: no STOP is sent, the TWI returns to unaddressed slave mode and releases SCL and SDA to high impedance.

fields.name: TWWC
fields.text: Set by a write to TWDR while TWINT is 0. Cleared by a write to TWDR while TWINT is 1.

fields.name: TWEN
fields.text: 1 turns on the TWI, which takes over the SCL and SDA pins and turns on their slew-rate limiters and spike filters. 0 switches the TWI off and ends every transmission at once, whatever is in progress.

fields.name: TWIE
fields.text: With this bit at 1 and SREG's I-bit set, the TWI interrupt request stays active as long as TWINT is 1.

fields.name: TWS
fields.text: Five-bit status of the TWI logic and the bus. A read of TWSR also returns the two prescaler bits; mask them to 0 to read the status independent of the prescaler.

fields.name: TWPS
fields.text: Bit rate prescaler, readable and writable; its value enters the bit rate equation.

fields.name: TWD
fields.text: The next byte to send, or the last byte received, on the bus.

fields.name: TWA
fields.text: The TWI unit's 7-bit slave address.

fields.name: TWGCE
fields.text: 1 turns on recognition of a general call on the bus.

fields.name: TWAM
fields.text: 7-bit mask on the slave address: a 1 in a bit makes address matching skip the comparison of that incoming address bit with the same bit of TWAR.

fields.name: ACD
fields.text: 1 cuts power to the Analog Comparator; it may be set at any time and lowers power use in Active and Idle modes. Clear ACIE before changing ACD, or an interrupt can occur on the change.

fields.name: ACBG
fields.text: 1: a fixed bandgap reference replaces the comparator's positive input. 0: AIN0 is the positive input. The bandgap voltage needs time to settle once selected; before it has, the first conversion may be wrong.

fields.name: ACO
fields.text: Comparator output after synchronization, which delays it by 1 to 2 clock cycles.

fields.name: ACI
fields.text: Hardware sets it when the comparator output does what ACIS1:0 selects. The comparator interrupt runs when ACIE and SREG's I-bit are set. Hardware clears it when the vector runs; writing 1 to it also clears it.

fields.name: ACIE
fields.text: 1, with SREG's I-bit set, turns the comparator interrupt on; 0 turns it off.

fields.name: ACIC
fields.text: 1 lets the comparator trigger Timer/Counter1's input capture: its output feeds the capture front end directly and uses that unit's noise canceler and edge select. 0: no link between the two. TIMSK1.ICIE1 must be set for the comparator to trigger the input capture interrupt.

fields.name: ACIS
fields.text: Chooses which comparator events trigger the interrupt. Clear ACIE before changing these bits, or an interrupt can occur on the change.

fields.name: AIN1D
fields.text: 1 turns off the digital input buffer on the AIN1 pin, and its PIN register bit then always reads 0. Set it when the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is unused, to save power in the buffer.

notes: Bit 7 is printed as MSB/IDRD.
The register summary prints bit 7 as OCDR7.

fields.name: IDRD
fields.text: I/O Debug Register Dirty.

fields.name: OCDR
fields.text: On-chip debug register data, bits 6:0.

fields.name: JTD
fields.text: 1 disables the JTAG interface; at 0 the interface is on when the JTAGEN fuse is programmed. A change takes effect only when the same value is written to the bit twice within four cycles. Leave it unchanged while On-chip Debug is in use.

fields.name: PUD
fields.text: 1 turns off the pull-up resistors on all I/O ports, even on pins whose DDxn and PORTxn settings ({DDxn, PORTxn} = 0b01) would enable one.

fields.name: IVSEL
fields.text: 0 puts the interrupt vectors at the start of Flash; 1 moves them to the start of the Boot Loader section, whose address the BOOTSZ fuses set. To change it, write IVCE to 1, then within four cycles write the new IVSEL value with IVCE at 0. Interrupts are off from the cycle IVCE is set until after the instruction that writes IVSEL, or for four cycles if IVSEL is not written; the I-bit in SREG is left as it is.

fields.name: IVCE
fields.text: Write 1 to allow a change of IVSEL; doing so turns interrupts off for the change sequence. Hardware clears it four cycles after the write or when IVSEL is written.

registers.title: MCU Status Register

Reading MCUSR and then clearing it early in the program lets the reset flags show the source of the next reset.

fields.name: JTRF
fields.text: Goes to 1 when the reset came from the JTAG Reset Register holding 1, that register being chosen by the AVR_RESET JTAG instruction. A Power-on Reset or a 0 written to the bit clears it.

fields.name: WDRF
fields.text: Goes to 1 after a Watchdog Reset. A Power-on Reset or a 0 written to the bit clears it.

fields.name: BORF
fields.text: Goes to 1 after a Brown-out Reset. A Power-on Reset or a 0 written to the bit clears it.

fields.name: EXTRF
fields.text: Goes to 1 after an External Reset. A Power-on Reset or a 0 written to the bit clears it.

fields.name: PORF
fields.text: Goes to 1 after a Power-on Reset. Only a 0 written to the bit clears it.

registers.name: SPMCSR
registers.title: Store Program Memory Control and Status Register

fields.name: SPMIE
fields.text: With this bit at 1 and SREG's I-bit set, the SPM ready interrupt is on; it runs for as long as SPMEN is 0.

fields.name: RWWSB
fields.text: Hardware sets it when self-programming (erasing or writing a page) of the RWW section begins; the RWW section cannot be accessed while it is 1. Cleared by writing RWWSRE to 1 after the self-programming is done, or automatically when a page load starts.

fields.name: SIGRD
fields.text: Written to 1 together with SPMEN, makes the next LPM within three clock cycles read a byte of the signature row into the destination register. An SPM within four cycles of setting SIGRD and SPMEN does nothing. Reserved for future use; not to be used.

fields.name: RWWSRE
fields.text: While a page in the RWW section is being erased or written, the section cannot be read (RWWSB is set). Once programming is done (SPMEN cleared), writing RWWSRE and SPMEN to 1 together makes the next SPM within four clock cycles re-enable the RWW section. It cannot be re-enabled while a page erase or page write is busy (SPMEN set). Writing RWWSRE while the Flash is being loaded aborts the load and the loaded data is lost.

fields.name: BLBSET
fields.text: Written to 1 together with SPMEN, makes the next SPM within four clock cycles set the Boot Lock bits from R0; R1 and the Z-pointer address are ignored. Clears itself when the lock bits are set, or when no SPM follows within four cycles. An (E)LPM within three cycles of setting BLBSET and SPMEN reads the Lock bits or the Fuse bits, chosen by Z0, into the destination register.

fields.name: PGWRT
fields.text: Written to 1 together with SPMEN, makes the next SPM within four clock cycles write the temporary buffer to the page addressed by the upper part of the Z-pointer; R1 and R0 are ignored. Clears itself when the page write finishes, or when no SPM follows within four cycles. The CPU halts for the whole page write when the NRWW section is addressed.

fields.name: PGERS
fields.text: Written to 1 together with SPMEN, makes the next SPM within four clock cycles erase the page addressed by the upper part of the Z-pointer; R1 and R0 are ignored. Clears itself when the page erase finishes, or when no SPM follows within four cycles. The CPU halts for the whole operation when the NRWW section is addressed.

fields.name: SPMEN
fields.text: Allows SPM for four clock cycles. If RWWSRE, BLBSET, PGWRT or PGERS is written with it, the next SPM carries out that operation. Written alone, the following SPM stores R1:R0 in the temporary page buffer at the Z-pointer address, ignoring the Z LSB. Clears itself when an SPM completes, or when none runs within four cycles; during page erase and page write it stays 1 until the operation is done. Writing any lower-five-bit pattern other than 10001, 01001, 00101, 00011 or 00001 has no effect. No more than one SPM at once.
